newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly defeats $2 bln bridge repair bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly defeats $2 bln bridge repair bill.

text.p: California lawmakers on Friday defeated a $2 billion bill to fund bridge improvements in the state without requiring toll increases.
The bill, by Republican Assemblyman Gary Miller, failed to clear the Democrat-controlled Assembly Appropriations Committee, Miller's office said.
Miller said his measure would have raised more than $2 billion to retrofit seven state toll bridges -- five in the San Francisco Bay area and two in southern California.
In contrast with proposals by San Francisco Bay area lawmakers, Miller said his legislation would not have "penalize the rest of the state" to fund Bay area bridge improvements.
Miller's legislation would have allocated $650 million in existing bond funds, $300 million in state gas taxes and $1.1 billion of existing toll bridge revenues to the projects.

The bill would not have required toll increases on any of the bridges. The assemblyman said enough money could be generated from existing tolls in the San Francisco Bay area to support bonds to fund the needed improvements.
